result.title: Beyond Hard Tokens: Predictive Memory for Multimodal Protein Generation
result.summary: Multimodal protein language models unify sequence and discrete structural tokens via iterative masked decoding, offering a promising paradigm for joint protein design. However, standard decoders rely on a memoryless mask reset at each iteration: only a sparse subset of newly committed hard tokens is carried forward, while all remaining unresolved sites are reset to an identical [MASK] embedding. In open-ended co-generation where neither modality provides a fixed external anchor, this stateless transition limits single-step refinement depth and deprives both tracks of stable cross-step soft anchors, leading to slow convergence or degenerative repetitive collapse. Observing that uncommitted predictions evolve with pronounced temporal coherence rather than erratic noise, we introduce Predictive Memory (PredMem), a training-free self-conditioning recurrence that carries these soft beliefs across steps. At each step, PredMem summarizes raw logits into a probability-weighted Top-$k$ expectation embedding at every residue and affinely interpolates it into eligible masked inputs on the next step at zero extra denoiser cost. Across DPLM-2, DPLM-2.1, and ESM3, PredMem raises unconditional sequence-structure co-generation success by 3.6, 17.7, and 48.7 percentage points, respectively, while improving the quality-diversity trade-off and suppressing repetitive mode collapse. Controlled diagnostics show that these gains stem primarily from early trajectory stabilization in unanchored cross-modal co-evolution rather than extra compute or simple entropy reduction, establishing PredMem as an efficient inference mechanism for multimodal discrete generation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对多模态蛋白质语言模型的迭代掩码解码，提出无需训练的 Predictive Memory：将每步未提交位置的原始 logits 压缩为概率加权 Top-k 期望嵌入，并插值回下一步的掩码输入，作为跨步软锚点，以缓解无外部锚的序列-结构共生成中收敛慢与重复坍缩。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「跨步携带软信念而非仅硬 token」的自条件递归，可为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的更新与跨步保持提供方法线索，可供核查该记忆是否被后续步骤实际使用、以及能否迁移到视觉-语言推理的中间状态。
